Scott Brister

Republican candidate for 15th Court of Appeals, Chief Justice, Texas

Chief Justice, Fifteenth Court of Appeals of Texas

Scott Brister is a Republican and the incumbent Chief Justice of the Fifteenth Court of Appeals of Texas. Gov. Greg Abbott appointed him as the court's first chief justice, effective September 1, 2024. He was unopposed in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary and faces Democrat Jerry Zimmerer in the November 3, 2026 general election, the first election for this seat.

Where Brister stands

Judicial philosophy
Says he will impartially follow the law as written and apply it faithfully and efficiently, and will not rule based on personal beliefs or political preferences.
Role of judges
Says judges should apply the law and not make laws, and pledges careful review and clear decisions based on the Constitution and written law.
Approach to decisions
His campaign website says his approach is to follow the law as written, respect the Constitution, and issue clear, reasoned decisions that stand the test of time.

Background

  • Chief Justice, Fifteenth Court of Appeals of Texas (appointed by Gov. Greg Abbott, effective Sept. 1, 2024–present)
  • Justice, Supreme Court of Texas (appointed 2003 by Gov. Rick Perry; elected 2004; served 2003–2009)
  • Justice and Chief Justice on Houston's First and Fourteenth Courts of Appeals
  • Judge, 234th District Court, Harris County
  • J.D., Harvard Law School (1980)
  • Undergraduate degree, Duke University
